study type: secondary analysis of a prospective observational study
outcome: self-reported impact of birth in daily life
need for psychosocial support after delivery
cohort: The study included 350 women with a history of spontaneous preterm birth (between 22 0/7 and 36 6/7 weeks of gestation) compared to 115 women who had a term birth.
finding: After a median of 13 years, no significant long-term differences were found in primary outcomes (depressive/anxiety symptoms, psychosocial distress), but women with a history of spontaneous preterm birth reported a greater impact of the birth in daily life, and those who needed but did not receive psychosocial support were at higher risk for anxiety and psychosocial distress.
gest_age: 22 0/7 and 36 6/7 weeks of gestation (for preterm births)
